solution: 0347: the hour the living-room clock stopped (3h47), which the diary calls 'the hour when the halves met'

clues.text: The house stands on Acacia Street, number 12
The watchmaker had lived alone since his daughter went abroad
The living-room wall clock stopped at 3h47 and was never set right again
The back door creaks when it rains
Poem on the desk: two halves that seek each other keep what matters
There is a collection of French stamps on the bookshelf
The study key was under the vase of sunflowers
The garden has two halves of flowerbed, one of roses and one of cabbages
The safe has four numbered brass dials
The house cat is called Pendulum
Diary: I hid the secret at the instant when everything stood still
Repair receipt for a clock, dated 12/05/1931
The butler's bedside clock was running five minutes fast
At the foot of the poem there is a yin-yang drawn in ink
The fireplace has not been lit for years
The neighbour heard chimes a little before four in the morning
A map of Switzerland hanging in the hallway
Electricity bill paid in 1931, on time
Letter to the daughter: remember Van Gogh's yellow when you come back
The portrait of his wife shows her holding an hourglass
Kitchen mug decorated with a painted sunflower
The watchmaker opened the workshop in 1931, according to the plaque
The butler says the master was fond of chess
In the drawer, a manual for valve radios
The last page of the diary was torn out
The piano is out of tune
Burnt fragment in the oven: '...when the halves met...'
Dust has gathered on the safe, except on the dials
The daughter sent a postcard from Lisbon
The watchmaker always set his appointments at odd hours

traps.why: the flowerbed's 'two halves': same expression, no relation
another clock, running fast, unrelated to the stop
1931 is the year of everything in the house, coincidence
